cases.question: Tell me about a production AI system you built and what you personally owned.
cases.answer: I owned a retrieval API from ingestion through monitoring, created the evaluation set, and reduced p95 latency by 30 percent.

cases.question: How did you evaluate whether the retrieval system was working well?
cases.answer: We tested it.

cases.question: What trade-off did you make when choosing the vector database?
cases.answer: I compared managed filtering and operational cost, then chose Postgres with pgvector because our scale did not justify another datastore.

cases.question: Describe a failure you encountered while deploying an agent workflow.
cases.answer: The first deployment looped after tool errors. I added a call budget, typed error states, and an escalation path, which eliminated runaway sessions.

cases.question: Which monitoring signals did you use after launch?
cases.answer: Latency and errors.

cases.question: How did you protect customer data in prompts?
cases.answer: I do not know; I would like to move on.

cases.question: How did you decide when an agent should call a tool?
cases.answer: Blue factory seven umbrella walks database quickly.

cases.question: What did you do when structured output validation failed?
cases.answer: I logged the validation code and retried once with the schema error, then failed closed instead of accepting an unverified answer.

cases.question: Tell me about a time an evaluation changed your design.
cases.answer: Groundedness fell on long documents, so I added section-aware chunking and reranking; the labeled pass rate rose from 71 to 86 percent.

cases.question: How did you handle duplicate background jobs?
cases.answer: We used idempotency keys and a unique database constraint around the external operation.

cases.question: Why did you choose FastAPI for that service?
cases.answer: It was good and Python was already there.

cases.question: What was the most difficult PostgreSQL performance issue you resolved?
cases.answer: A tenant-scoped query scanned a large events table. I added the matching composite index and verified the plan and p95 before rollout.

cases.question: How did you control model cost in production?
cases.answer: I routed simple extraction to a smaller model, capped tokens, cached stable prompts, and tracked cost per completed workflow.

cases.question: Describe how you tested concurrency before release.
cases.answer: I sent some requests and watched the server.

cases.question: How did you recover from a queue backlog?
cases.answer: I cannot recall that incident well enough to answer, so please continue to the next question.

cases.question: What was your role in the API migration?
cases.answer: I designed the compatibility layer, migrated two consumers, and owned the rollback plan; the team completed the cutover without downtime.

cases.question: How did you measure speech-to-text quality?
cases.answer: I used word error rate on accented and noisy interview clips, then reviewed named entities separately because they affected scoring evidence.

cases.question: What would you improve in your previous agent architecture?
cases.answer: The orchestration.

cases.question: How did you prevent one tenant from consuming all inference capacity?
cases.answer: I applied global and per-tenant admission limits, returned explicit capacity errors, and measured queue time instead of silently falling back.

cases.question: Tell me about a technical decision you reversed.
cases.answer: After load tests showed our agent framework added unnecessary calls, I replaced that path with a bounded state machine and cut median turn latency by 22 percent.
